transcript.text: vax upright brush thingy stopped spinnin, sucks ok thru the hose but nt pickin up off carpet. smelt like burnin rubber b4 it stopped

That burning smell followed by the brush stopping usually points to a mechanical issue in the floorhead rather than the main suction motor. The most common cause is the drive belt snapping (which releases the tension and stops the spin) or something like hair/thread jamming the roller so tight it overheats the motor. Please unplug the vacuum first for safety. Turn the floorhead over and inspect the brush bar area. Check if there is any debris wrapped around the roller that might be jamming it, and look to see if the rubber drive belt inside the base is still present and tight on the pulleys, or if it has snapped or slipped off.
ok unplugged n turned it over. brushbar turns by hand but its tight, theres loads of hair n a tassel wrapped round the ends

[Heading: Brush bar jammed by debris]
That confirms why it stopped: the hair and tassel jammed the brush bar, forcing the motor to work against a blockage until it overheated (the burning smell) and likely triggered a safety cut-out. Please carefully cut away and remove all the debris from the brush bar ends and bristles. Once clear, spin the bar by hand; it should now turn freely. If it still feels tight or doesn't spin easily, check if the rubber drive belt inside the base is still intact and on its pulleys, or if it has snapped due to the strain.
ok cut the hair n tassel off, spins free by hand now. what next?

[Heading: Drive belt likely snapped or slipped off]
The strain from the jam often snaps the drive belt or makes it slip off its pulley. Please check inside the base plate: if the belt is there and tight, try plugging it in and tilting the vacuum back to see if the brush spins (this tests the motor). If the belt is missing, broken, or loose, that’s your fault—replace the belt. If the belt is fine but the brush still doesn't spin when powered, the brush-bar motor has likely failed from the overheating.
ok took the sole plate off, belt is snapped in 2 bits, one bit has a shiny melted lookin edge. so need a new belt?

⚠ Stop using this appliance
A burning smell or smoke can mean an electrical fault or a fire risk. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it (or turn it off at the fuse box), and don't run it again — not even as a test — until it has been checked by a qualified engineer. Switch it off and unplug it (or take the battery off) first. Yes, that confirms the fault. The jamming caused the motor to work against a blockage until it overheated and snapped the belt (the melted edge is from that friction heat). You need to replace the drive belt. Once fitted, put the base plate back on, plug the vacuum in, tilt it back, and check that the brush spins freely when you switch it on.
